title: Same panels, different envelope

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: An empty assembled object includes a large hollow in its envelope. Stacking the ideal panels removes that hollow from the outside dimensions while retaining all panel material.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

claims.text: Assembled, the envelope includes the empty hollow: about 40 × 40 × 40 = 64,000 cm³. Stacked, the panels take 40 × 40 × 6 = 9,600 cm³. The material is the same; the hollow is gone. Only dismantle furniture its instructions allow.

recall.question: An empty cube is built from 6 panels, each 40 × 40 × 1 cm. Roughly what is its outside volume assembled, and with the panels stacked flat?
recall.why: Assembled, the envelope includes the empty hollow: about 40 × 40 × 40 = 64,000 cm³. Stacked, the panels take 40 × 40 × 6 = 9,600 cm³. The material is the same; the hollow is gone. Only dismantle furniture its instructions allow.
